sara: Heads-up — after the 08:12 runtime deploy we saw ~18% throughput drop for continuous batching when requests include tool/function calls that emit structured JSON and explicit stop tokens. Repro on staging with synthetic load. Logs show lots of `pause_for_tool` events that block decode batching.

matt: Can you paste the perf trace? curious if it's KV or kernel selection.

sara: Perf snippet from perf-bot:```
decode_loop_ms/token: 12.4 -> 15.1
batch_size_avg: 8.0 -> 5.1
kv_cache_hit: 0.87 -> 0.86
kernel_switches: FP16->Q8 fallback increased by 22%
pause_for_tool_events: 320/min -> 910/min
```

ali: Interesting — KV hit rate roughly same, so not cache coldness. Looks like batching fragmentation: when a tool call occurs mid-decode we do a pause which forces partial batches to flush early. stop tokens + structured outputs cause earlier end-of-sequence detection and more ragged batch formation.

jin: So two impacts: (1) token-budget scheduler currently treats tool pause as terminal, so it reduces max tokens per batch for waiting requests, (2) kernel selection oscillations when batches shrink cause slower qkernel fallback decisions — overhead per-switch.

matt: Quick experiment idea: mark tool pauses as "soft pause" with expected_remaining_tokens estimate; keep request in batch if expected_remaining_tokens <= 32. Also try age_weighted queue policy to favor older requests assembling full batches.

perf-bot: Ran canary on staging with `token_budget=128` + `soft_pause_threshold=32` + `queue_policy=age_weighted` for 10m. Result:```
batch_size_avg: 7.2 (was 5.1)
throughput_tokens/s: +14%
p99_latency: +6% (still within SLO)
kernel_switches: -12%
pause_events: -45%
```

ali: Nice. The p99 bump is expected since we hold some requests longer to assemble bigger batches. Tradeoff looks reasonable for most customers.

jin: Also saw fewer tool-triggered context switches. Suggest adding micro-heuristic: if structured output length < 48 bytes or returns `tool_fast=true` hint, treat as non-blocking. We can expose that via function-call schema: `tool_call_meta: {expect_tokens: int, fast: bool}`.

sara: We should be careful with opaque third-party tools. Default to conservative (soft pause) unless tool explicitly marks `fast=true`. Default threshold = 32 tokens.

matt: Kernel side — we should avoid re-querying kernel selectors on every tiny batch change. Cache kernel choice per-model sequence-length-bucket for 1s. That reduced kernel_switch overhead in perf-bot run.

perf-bot: Additional note: disabling immediate stop-token flush (treat stop as end-of-turn but allow finishing batch window 10ms) improved batch coalescing. Combined change further recovered throughput.

ali: Action items: 1) implement soft-pause + tool hint in runtime (sara/jin) 2) add kernel selection short-lived cache (matt) 3) add queue_policy=age_weighted as default for toolcall-heavy traffic (prod config) 4) add e2e perf test for structured outputs (perf team).

jin: I'll kick off a canary with 10% traffic, monitor cost metrics. If p99 stays within 1.2x and throughput improves, we roll.

sara: I'll add a small doc block in `runtime/queue.md` and include the heuristics we tested + commands to reproduce:```
# reproduce locally
./bin/loadgen --pattern toolcall_structured --qps 120 --duration 600 \\
  --token_budget 128 --queue_policy age_weighted --soft_pause_threshold 32
```

matt: Thanks — great triage. If we still see regressions for very large structured outputs we can fall back to per-request routing to dedicated capacity.

perf-bot: Canary started at 08:47. Will post summary at 09:10. :robot_face:

sara: tagging @oncall in case we need to roll back quickly. :eyes:
